body: Three specific problems. (1) The load-bearing assumption that Materials Project provides thermal conductivity tensors is almost certainly false — MP hosts DFT formation energies, band structures, and elastic tensors, but not k_x/k_y/k_z thermal conductivity values; the entire P1 pipeline ('queries for materials with known thermal conductivity values') and SC-003 are untestable as written, and the gap analysis's claim of a first dataset rests on it. (2) Average shortest path length on a periodic crystal graph is not a meaningful topological descriptor: it is dominated by the arbitrary choice of unit cell (a supercell of the same crystal yields different path lengths), so any correlation found with it may be an artifact of cell size rather than physics. The spec never addresses periodic boundary conditions or cell-size normalization. (3) There are drafting defects: lines 53-58 contain leftover editing instructions ('The specific value to remove/generalize: k... Rewritten passage:') embedded mid-scenario, and SC-002 specifies 'stratified cross-validation' while FR-007 specifies plain k-fold — for a continuous regression target, stratification is undefined, so the two requirements conflict.
